readme: recipe-floor-id -> board-commodity-id mappings for derive-recipe-floors.ps1. EVERY entry is a ONE-TIME HUMAN VERIFICATION that the two ids are the SAME commodity in the SAME form (fresh vs frozen, block vs shredded, plain vs seasoned all count as DIFFERENT). A verified entry automates that row's monthly floor refresh forever; a wrong one silently prices the floor off a different product (the board-collision class). Add entries as the monthly agent hand-checks the no-board-match list; include reviewed dates.
review_log: 2026-07-23: 16 mappings accepted from propose-floor-id-map.ps1 evidence gate (full label-token match + unit reconciliation + multi-store price agreement <=25%) with human review of each; REJECTED olives->olive-oil (single-token false positive, different product) - see out/floor-id-map-proposals.json for the evidence rows. pepperoncini->banana-peppers verified intentional: the board commodity label is literally Banana Peppers / Pepperoncini. ROUND 2 (2026-07-23): 17 more accepted via curated price-test (>=2-store everyday agreement + form review). REJECTED with evidence: boneless-skinless-chicken-thigh->chicken-thighs (board=bone-in drumstick pricing, 1/6), jasmine-rice->rice (0/6, jasmine pricier), salsa-verde->salsa (1/5), seasoned-black-beans->canned-black-beans (1/4), 93-7-ground-turkey->ground-turkey (3 stores cheapest = fattier grind, would understate), red-bell-pepper->bell-peppers (board cheapest = green), zero-sugar-soda-2l->soda (2L vs 12-pack economics), frozen-broccoli-florets->frozen-broccoli (cuts-vs-florets understating risk). apple->apples accepted on identity; its each-vs-lb unit mismatch is the deriver's refusal flow, safe. ROUND 3 (2026-08-02, monthly refresh): 7 pairs vetted against candidates-2026-08-01, 2 ACCEPTED. 93-7-ground-beef->ground-beef-93-7: a pure id-naming variant - same label semantics, same unit (lb), and the row items were ALREADY 93/7 products at every store; everyday agreement 5/5 within 5% (Aldi 0.987, Walmart 0.95, Sam's 1.00, Hy-Vee 1.00, Family Fare 1.00; Baker's has no everyday candidate and keeps its prior value). olives->black-olives: the board label is literally 'Black Olives (canned, ripe)' and every row item was already a black ripe canned olive; 3/3 EXACT agreement on shared cells (Sam's, Baker's, Hy-Vee all 1.00), Aldi 1.152 replaces an UNIDENTIFIED frozen 0.23 with an identified board observation, and it fills a previously EMPTY Walmart cell. Also lifts olives off the second-class recipe pool. REJECTED with evidence this round: breadcrumbs->bread-crumbs (the board commodity is the COMBINED 'Bread Crumbs / Panko' and its cheapest member is PLAIN/Italian crumbs while every recipe row item is PANKO - Walmart 0.373, Family Fare 0.361, Baker's 0.383 of current: the golden-raisins failure exactly); honey-dijon-mustard->honey-mustard (the board mixes salad DRESSING with condiment mustard - Family Fare 0.3893 -> 0.2288 by swapping a 10.25 oz condiment for a 24 fl oz Ken's dressing, with fl oz vs oz on top); corn-tortillas->tortillas (board label is literally 'Tortillas (flour)', every board pick is flour, 1.5x-3.1x divergence); swiss-cheese->sliced-cheese (every board pick is AMERICAN singles, 0.59-0.80 of current); canned-sweet-corn->canned-corn (identity is PERFECT - literally the same whole-kernel cans at Aldi/Walmart/Baker's - but the row is per-DRAINED-CAN 'each' while the board is per-oz, and meal-prep/db/bid-decisions-2026-07-26.json already records that 'the canned-sweet-corn per-each drained-can basis is a separate calibration issue', so mapping it would only convert a clean no-match into a refused unit-mismatch while inviting someone to 'fix' the unit and break drained-can cost math. Revisit WITH that calibration, not before). Not re-proposed: the ids already rejected in rounds 1-2 and the 2 retired below.

retired.golden-raisins: was 'raisins'. REMOVED 2026-08-01: a FORM violation of this file's own rule. The board's raisins commodity is dark seedless; deriving from it priced golden raisins off 'Our Family Seedless Raisins' and 'Smart Way Seedless Raisins', dropping Family Fare 0.57 -> 0.2995/oz and Baker's 0.4158 -> 0.2408. Golden raisins genuinely cost more. The frozen 2026-07-12 hand-browse is the RIGHT product at a stale price, which beats the WRONG product at a fresh one.
retired.hot-italian-sausage: was 'italian-sausage'. REMOVED 2026-08-01: a FORM violation. Deriving from the generic commodity picked 'Marketside MILD Italian Sausage' at Walmart (4.98 -> 2.5011/lb) and 'Kroger SWEET Italian Sausage' at Baker's (4.88 -> 3.5467). Hot vs mild vs sweet is the same 'plain vs seasoned' distinction this file already calls DIFFERENT.
